HubSpot Company Record — Altitude Defense (ID: 12117)

Overview
- Gov-adjacent defense contractor / systems integrator. Building internal LLM workflows for incident analysis + document triage.
- Primary ask: Private deployment with SIEM-ready audit export into their internal monitoring stack.
- They are explicitly NOT comfortable with sending audit logs to a vendor-managed endpoint. Needs to run in their environment.

What they want from Redwood
- Private deployment (air-gapped / restricted network): Kubernetes-based install.
- Audit logging + export that is SIEM-ready:
  - Strong delivery guarantees: at-least-once acceptable if we provide clear dedupe guidance and replay controls.
  - Explicit failure states + operator visibility (paused/degraded/backlog, last success, last error).
  - Filtering to reduce noise: by event_type, actor, workspace/tenant, and environment.
- Export destination requirements:
  - S3-compatible sink to internal object storage (MinIO mentioned; they also said "S3-compatible is fine as long as SDK works").
  - Encryption: customer-managed keys (SSE-KMS equivalent) and/or bucket-level encryption policy; they will own keys.
  - Partitioning: by tenant + time (hourly ok) for downstream ingestion; wants predictable naming.

Security/compliance notes (evaluation)
- They asked for: threat model summary for "exporting audit logs to customer-managed endpoints" and details on credential handling/rotation.
- Key quote from security lead: "Duplicates are OK; silent drops are not." They want strong visibility into backlog and retry behavior.
- They want a clear statement of delivery semantics (at-least-once) and recommended dedupe strategy.
- They will require SSO/SAML for Console access in their environment and tight RBAC around who can configure export destinations.

Current product fit assessment
- SIEM-ready audit export (beta) aligns, but only via S3 sink for this account (Splunk HEC + Datadog intake are not viable without egress).
- Private install dependency: audit-export control-plane service + worker subsystem must be supported in Private installer/helm with documented network egress = none (except internal endpoints).

Artifacts shared / referenced (internal)
- Audit Event Schema v1 reference (requested for parsing + correlation fields): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v1.json
- Delivery semantics decision record (requested by security): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0217-audit-export-delivery-semantics.json
- S3 sink partitioning/encryption ADR (requested by platform team): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0219-s3-sink-partitioning-and-encryption.json
- Private install notes stub (shared as draft): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/private-siem-export-install-notes.json

Open questions / risks
- S3-compatible endpoint details: they want to confirm MinIO/Ceph compatibility (path-style vs virtual-hosted style, TLS requirements, region handling).
- KMS/HSM: need to validate how we configure encryption in their object store environment (SSE-KMS analog vs client-side encryption). They asked whether we can support key rotation without downtime.
- Replay safeguards: they asked for guardrails (time-window limits, explicit confirmation, audit trail of replays).
- Beta acceptance: they want the beta limitations written down (no guarantee of historical backfill for all tenants; duplicates possible; initial sinks limited).

Next steps (owner + SE)
- Colin O'Donnell to schedule architecture review with their platform/security teams; include Marcus Lin (schema/security), Kevin Osei (SIEM export security), and Diego Santos (private deployment engineering) if available.
- Fatima Noor to send: (1) schema v1 + example events, (2) S3 sink details incl. partitioning + encryption options, (3) operational posture (SLOs/runbooks) at a high level.
- Confirm whether they will be a beta design partner for SIEM-ready audit export in Private (feature flag + controlled rollout).

Internal notes (shorthand)
- “Air-gapped means air-gapped.” They will not whitelist external SIEM endpoints.
- They care more about audit completeness + provable delivery than raw latency.
- Procurement will hinge on: Private installer readiness + audit export operability + security review evidence package.
